pageCache.text:
After School Clubs and After School Care Club
Covid-19 - Risk Assessments for SCL After School Care Club
After School Care - SCL
Here at Old Basing Infant School we work with SCL to provide after school care on site from 3.15pm-6.00pm every school day. This care will be open to children from Old Basing Infant School and St. Mary's Junior School. The care will provide a variety of activities for children to enjoy. Booking for the provision will be online and directly with SCL. More information can be found here: https://sclactive.co.uk/
Alongside the after school care we will continue to provide a range of hour long after school clubs with Sports Xtra, Linguatastic and others. These clubs will be open to new Year R children from October half term and for Year 1 and 2 from September. Information on the clubs available will be circulated to parents each half term and information can also be provided by the school office.
Children who attend the after school clubs will also be able to access the after school care as a bolt- on after their club finishes.
More details on after school clubs, costs and provision available are circulated each half term allowing parents to sign their child up for the clubs they are interested in.
Click on the links below to see the exciting activities that are happening in our school.

Our Vision and Values
School Vision and Values 2025

If you would like to view this content please Accept All Manage Cookies
Courage to Try, Power to Change
Our mission is to foster a school community where courage allows us to face challenges, kindness shapes our relationships, and resilience empowers us to overcome difficulty. We strive to collaborate with one another, embracing curiosity to continuously learn and grow. With respect as our foundation, we aim to create an environment that uplifts and inspires each individual to thrive, both personally and collectively.
Kindness - We all need kindness and above all we want our children to recognise the power of kindness to build relationships, to interactive positively with others and to support each other. Kindness is the value that allows our children to develop resilience and in turn courage. It is perhaps one of our most important values because of the impact that it has on all the others.
Respect—We aim for children to have respect for themselves and others, for property and the environment; in order to enable everyone to thrive and have a positive place within our community. We want our children to respect the right of all individuals to be themselves and to celebrate our similarities alongside the things that make us unique and different.
Courage – Courage allows children to take risks that are carefully considered but that may be a little scary. It allows our children to be open to challenge in the knowledge that although learning can be hard at times it is hugely but rewarding when we try something new or persevere with a challenge. With the courage to try, who knows what may be possible and what our children can achieve.
Resilience - We want our children to be resilient, flexible and adaptable in order to learn in a range of different ways. We aim for all our children to develop resilience so that they can learn from things that don't go their way, negotiate friendships and relationships and move forward with confidence and independence. We want our children to know that when things don't go their way, that it is ok, it is part of the learning process and that they can have another go!
Curiosity – Children are curious as are all human beings. To be curious is to discover and move forward. Curious children discover, learn, invent, design and imagine. For the future that is unknown we want to build curiosity in our children to ensure they have a bright future with endless possibilities, limited only by their imaginations.
Collaboration – Through collaboration we can learn more and achieve more together. We want our children to grow as learners and into adults who are able to adapt their skills and working and learning styles to match new and different contexts. By collaborating with others who work or think differently, we learn a new perspective and discover more. Working together children can learn from each other and take their learning on every day.

pageCache.text:
British Values
British values are a set of core principles promoted in the UK, encompassing Democracy, Rule of Law, Individual Liberty, and Mutual Respect and Tolerance for diverse faiths and beliefs. These values are promoted at Old Basing Infants through our mission statement, values, inclusive and diverse curriculum and our rights respecting education.
Our mission statement below encompasses all of the British values;
to foster a school community where courage allows us to face challenges, kindness shapes our relationships, and resilience empowers us to overcome difficulty. We strive to collaborate with one another, embracing curiosity to continuously learn and grow. With respect as our foundation, we aim to create an environment that uplifts and inspires each individual to thrive, both personally and collectively.
The document below shows how each value is embedded through our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Old Basing Infant School - Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
The school operates a Breakfast Club that is open to families with children at Old Basing Infant School and St. Mary's Junior School.
The club runs from 7:45am to 8:35am in the school hall and, when the weather allows, on the school field. The charge is currently £5.00 per session. Children can arrive anytime within the Breakfast Club period, but breakfast will only be provided to children who arrive before 8:15am. The charge will be the same whatever time children arrive.
The numbers are limited and so places must be booked in advance. Children cannot turn up without a booking having been made. Bookings should be made at least 24 hours ahead. Any non attendance will not be refunded unless the school is aware of an illness or other emergency situation.
Breakfasts of cereal and toast with milk or water to drink will be provided, with other options being offered on an occasional basis, such as crumpets, muffins or porridge.
Children who attend St. Mary's Junior School are escorted to the junior school at 8:35am by Breakfast Club staff.
If you would like to access the Breakfast Club for your child, please speak to a member of the office staff who will be able to help you.

Our Curriculum
What does your child learn at school each day? Children at Old Basing Infant School follow the National Curriculum for Early Years Foundation Stage and for Key Stage 1. We teach in a topic-led way, allowing children to makes links in their learning between different curriculum areas as much as possible. Where links cannot be made we teach discreet units of work. To find out more about our curriculum follow the links below which will give you a greater insight into how we teach and what we teach.
